metaDescription: Six meal prep container sets compared on compartments, glass versus plastic, 4 cup portions, lid design and piece counts, from Bentgo to Vtopmart glass.
introParagraphs: Meal prep only works if the containers make Sunday easier and Wednesday lunch simple. That means portions you can judge by eye, lids that stay closed in a bag, and a material you trust in the microwave and freezer. The big decision is glass or plastic, followed by one compartment or three.

This comparison covers six distinct picks: the 20 piece Bentgo Prep set with three compartments, the single compartment GoodCook 10 pack, the KOMUEE 10 pack of 30 ounce borosilicate glass, the Vtopmart 5 pack of 22 ounce glass, the Rubbermaid Brilliance Tritan set, and the Dealusy 50 pack at 32 ounces. We left out the single compartment Bentgo variant and the 24 ounce Dealusy because they duplicate a pick already listed.

We evaluated each set based on product specs and buyer feedback on its listing, not on a lab bench. Where a listing does not state a detail such as lid heat limits, we tell you to check the product page.

products.name: Bentgo Prep 3 Compartment Meal Prep Containers, 20 Piece
products.description:
The Bentgo Prep 3 compartment set is built for portion controlled meals. It is a 20 piece set with a 4 cup capacity and embossed measurements, and the listing says the material is PFAS and BPA free. Three compartments keep a protein, a grain and a vegetable from touching.

The stackable, lightweight design makes the set easy to carry to work, and the listing describes it as durable and reusable. The tradeoff is flexibility: a divided tray is awkward for soup or a large casserole slice. The excerpt does not state microwave or dishwasher limits, so check the product page before heating.

It is the pick for people who plan balanced meals and want visual portions. Compared with the GoodCook at one compartment, it keeps foods separate, and compared with the Rubbermaid Brilliance, it ships as a larger set. If you want glass, the KOMUEE at 10 pack is the closer match.
products.bestFor: Balanced portioned meals where foods should stay separate.
pros: PFAS and BPA free per listing
cons: Dividers limit soups and large portions
Heating limits not stated in the excerpt

products.name: GoodCook Meal Prep Containers, Single Compartment 10 Pack
products.description:
The GoodCook set is the plain, practical choice. It includes ten containers with ten lids, each with a single compartment embossed with 4 cup volume measurements for portion control. The listing says the BPA free containers are dishwasher, freezer and microwave safe, and stackable.

A single open compartment handles bowls, pasta, stir fries and soups better than a divided tray. The tradeoff is that foods mix unless you separate them yourself, and the excerpt does not describe how securely the lid seals. Check the product page for leak details before packing liquids in a bag.

It suits a household that preps one big dish at a time. Compared with the Bentgo 3 compartment set, it gives a single open space, and compared with the KOMUEE glass at 30 ounces, it is lighter. Its markings make it easy to portion by the cup.
products.bestFor: Simple weekly meal prep in a single open compartment.
cons: Lid seal details not in the excerpt

products.name: KOMUEE 10 Pack 30 oz Glass Meal Prep Containers
products.description:
The KOMUEE set gives you ten glass meal prep containers at 30 ounces, each with a plastic lid. The listing describes borosilicate glass and says it is stronger than cheaper glass storage. It can be used in the microwave, freezer and dishwasher.

Glass resists stains and odors, which helps with tomato sauce and curry. The tradeoff is weight, and the lids are plastic, so check lid heat guidance on the product page. Ten glass containers are also heavy to carry compared with plastic sets.

This is the set for people who want glass at a 10 pack scale. At 30 ounces each it is larger than the Vtopmart glass at 22 ounces, and it comes in twice the count. Compared with the Bentgo and GoodCook sets, it is heavier but more resistant to staining.
products.bestFor: Prepping a week of meals in stain resistant glass.
cons: Heavy to carry compared with plastic
Plastic lids need heat limit checks

products.name: Vtopmart 5 Pack 22 oz Glass Meal Prep Containers
products.description:
The Vtopmart 5 pack is a smaller glass set with a standout lid. Each of the five containers holds 22 ounces, and the hinged lid flips open and shut with a snap seal described as airtight and leakproof. The listing says the glass is safe for the oven, microwave, dishwasher and freezer.

The oven rating is the main reason to pick it over plastic: you can reheat in the same dish you stored in. The tradeoff is that five containers cover fewer days than a 10 pack, and the excerpt does not state lid heat limits, so check the product page before heating with the lid on.

It works well for office lunch or a short prep week. At 22 ounces it is smaller than the KOMUEE at 30 ounces, with half the count. Compared with the GoodCook, it is heavier but handles oven reheating.

Hinged snap lids flip open easily

products.name: Rubbermaid Brilliance Tritan Food Storage Containers
products.description:
The Rubbermaid Brilliance line is made of crystal clear Tritan plastic that the listing describes as stain resistant and odor resistant. It uses airtight lids with secure latches and a seal described as 100 percent leak proof. The listing calls it lightweight and sturdy, and suitable for lunch and meal prep.

Tritan is a hard, clear plastic, so you can see what is inside without opening the lid. The tradeoff is that the excerpt does not list the piece count or capacities, so check the product page to see which set you are buying. It also does not state microwave or dishwasher limits.

It is a good pick for a premium plastic that looks tidy in the fridge. Compared with the GoodCook, the latches add a stronger seal, and compared with glass sets like the KOMUEE, it is much lighter. The Bentgo trades clarity for compartments.
products.bestFor: Tidy, clear plastic prep that carries easily.
pros: Clear Tritan lets you see contents
Stain and odor resistant per listing
cons: Piece count not in the excerpt
Heating limits not in the excerpt

products.name: Dealusy 50 Pack 32 oz Meal Prep Containers
products.description:
The Dealusy 50 pack is a high volume plastic set. It has 50 containers at 32 ounces each with 50 lids, 100 pieces in total, and the lids are described as easy open. The listing says the thick plastic is leakproof and stackable, safe for the microwave and freezer, and BPA free.

The listing also calls the containers disposable, which means they are meant to be light and low maintenance. The tradeoff is durability: thin plastic wears faster than glass or Tritan, and fifty containers take serious storage room. Check the product page for dishwasher guidance.

It makes sense for batch cooking or sharing meals. At 32 ounces each it is larger than the KOMUEE at 30 ounces and the Vtopmart at 22 ounces, and the count dwarfs the GoodCook at 10. Compared with the Rubbermaid Brilliance, it is far less premium but far higher in volume.
products.bestFor: Big batch cooking and giving meals away.
pros: 32 oz size fits a full meal
Microwave and freezer safe per listing
cons: Thin plastic wears faster than glass
Needs a lot of storage space

buyingCriteria.explanation: Divided trays keep foods separate, which matters for crisp vegetables next to saucy protein. The Bentgo Prep 3 compartment set at 4 cups is the clear divider choice. For soups, stews and pasta, a single compartment like the GoodCook 10 pack is easier. Pick based on what you cook most, because a divider that does not fit your food becomes a nuisance. A practical test is to picture your three most common dinners and ask whether each would fit without crowding. The Bentgo at 4 cups gives roughly a cup and a third per section if you split evenly, so bulky foods like roasted vegetables may feel tight.

Glass resists stains and odors and can often go in the oven, as the Vtopmart 5 pack does. Plastic is lighter, which matters if you carry lunches daily. The KOMUEE at 30 ounces in glass is heavy across ten containers, while the Bentgo and GoodCook sets are much lighter. Check lid heat limits either way, because most glass sets use plastic lids. Weigh a loaded glass container in your hand before committing to a full set. Ten KOMUEE containers stacked in a tote bag add up, while ten GoodCook containers barely register, and that difference shows up in your shoulder by Friday.

A container that is too big encourages bigger servings, and one that is too small forces two. The Bentgo and GoodCook sets mark 4 cups, the KOMUEE holds 30 ounces, the Vtopmart holds 22 ounces and the Dealusy holds 32 ounces. For a standard lunch, 22 to 30 ounces usually fits a protein and side. Match the size to your appetite and your plan. If you eat out of the container, a wider shape is easier to use than a tall narrow one. The 22 ounce Vtopmart suits a side dish and protein, while the 32 ounce Dealusy has room for a full bowl of pasta with sauce.

Meal prep containers ride in bags, so the lid matters. The Vtopmart 5 pack uses hinged snap lids described as airtight and leakproof, and the Rubbermaid Brilliance uses latches described as 100 percent leak proof. The Dealusy lids are easy open, which is convenient but may be less secure for soup. Test with water before carrying liquids. A quick home test is to fill a container with water, close the lid, and tip it upside down over the sink for a few seconds. Do this with every new set before you trust it in a bag with a laptop.

Meal prep means microwaves and freezers, so check what each material allows. The GoodCook lists microwave, freezer and dishwasher, and the Dealusy lists microwave and freezer. The Vtopmart 5 pack adds the oven. Where the excerpt is silent, such as for the Bentgo and Rubbermaid, check the product page rather than assuming. Freezer use adds one more consideration, which is leaving headroom for expansion. Soups and sauces grow as they freeze, so fill a 30 ounce KOMUEE or 32 ounce Dealusy to about three quarters, and let food cool before sealing it.

More containers means fewer washes, but they take space. The Dealusy at 50 pieces is the extreme end, the KOMUEE and GoodCook at 10 are comfortable for a week, and the Vtopmart at 5 is a small start. Count your meals per week and add a few for rotation. Nesting or stackable designs, as with the Bentgo, save room. Also think about how often you will wash. Fewer, bigger sets such as the 50 pack mean you can cook once and wash rarely, while a 10 pack like the GoodCook pushes you into a weekly wash cycle that keeps containers fresher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Layout and portions
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each listing for compartments and measurement markings. The Bentgo Prep leads on dividers with three compartments, while the GoodCook uses a single compartment with 4 cup marks. Portion tools such as embossed measurements counted in a pick's favor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material and heat use
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared glass, Tritan and plastic by what the maker states. The Vtopmart 5 pack lists oven, microwave, freezer and dishwasher, the KOMUEE lists microwave, freezer and dishwasher, and the GoodCook adds dishwasher with microwave and freezer. Silent listings were scored conservatively.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lid and leak design
howWeEvaluated.description: Lids were judged on the design the listing describes. The Vtopmart hinged snap lid and the Rubbermaid Brilliance latches rank highest on stated leak protection. The Dealusy easy open lid trades some security for convenience.

howWeEvaluated.title: Count and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how much you get. The Dealusy leads at 50 containers and 32 ounces, the KOMUEE gives ten at 30 ounces, and the Vtopmart gives five at 22 ounces. The Bentgo gives a 20 piece set.

howWeEvaluated.title: Carry and care
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed weight, stackability and cleaning. Plastic sets like the Bentgo and GoodCook are lighter to carry, and glass sets like the KOMUEE are heavier but resist stains. Stated dishwasher safety counted.

howToChoose.intro: Pick the layout that matches how you eat.
howToChoose.note: Choose the layout first and the material second, since a container that does not fit your meals will sit unused no matter how well it is made.
A lower tier set is not a worse set. The GoodCook and Bentgo cover most weekday needs, and the glass picks are for people who reheat in the oven or dislike plastic staining.

howToChoose.intro: The core tradeoff in this lineup.

cards.label: Glass
cards.text: Glass resists stains and odors and can often go in the oven. The KOMUEE 10 Pack and Vtopmart 5 Pack are the glass picks here, and both use plastic lids. Choose glass if you reheat a lot and do not mind weight.

cards.label: Plastic
cards.text: Plastic is lighter and cheaper to carry daily, as with the Bentgo Prep, GoodCook, Rubbermaid Brilliance Tritan and Dealusy. It can stain over time. Choose plastic for commuting and bulk.

howToChoose.intro: Where the meal gets eaten shapes the container.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Five to ten containers, a size between 22 and 32 ounces, a leak resistant lid and heat limits that match your reheating. Embossed markings help portion.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The GoodCook and KOMUEE at ten each cover a full week, the Bentgo at 20 pieces covers ten meals, and the Vtopmart at five covers a short week.

faq.q: Should I choose glass or plastic?
faq.a: Choose glass if you hate stained containers, with the KOMUEE 10 Pack and Vtopmart 5 Pack as the glass options. Choose plastic if you carry lunch daily, with the GoodCook, Bentgo and Dealusy sets. Weight is the main tradeoff. Many people end up with one of each, using glass at home and plastic for transport. If you only buy one set, think about where most of your meals will be eaten.

faq.q: Are three compartments better than one?
faq.a: Only if your meals suit dividers. The Bentgo Prep 3 compartment set keeps foods separate, but a single compartment like the GoodCook handles soups and pasta better. Pick the layout that matches your usual meal.

faq.q: How many containers do I need?
faq.a: Count meals per week and add a few for rotation. Ten containers, as in the GoodCook or KOMUEE sets, cover a standard five day lunch and dinner plan. The Vtopmart at five covers a short week, and the Dealusy at 50 is for large batches. Choosing a set with enough pieces, such as the Dealusy 50 pack or the Bentgo 20 piece set, is what keeps a clean container available for each prep day.

faq.q: Can I microwave with the lid on?
faq.a: Not unless the product page says so. The listings state microwave safety for several sets, but lid heat limits are usually not stated. Vent or remove the lid to be safe.

faq.q: How long does prepped food last?
faq.a: That depends on the food, not the container. Follow standard refrigerator guidance for cooked meals and freeze portions you will not eat soon. The freezer safe sets such as the GoodCook and Dealusy make freezing simple. Label each lid with the cooking date so nothing lingers in the back of the fridge.

faq.q: Do disposable style containers work for reuse?
faq.a: The Dealusy listing calls the containers disposable and also reusable. Thin plastic wears faster than glass or Tritan, so treat it as a short term set. Check the product page for dishwasher advice before reusing.

Tomato and curry pigments soak into plastic over time. Tritan, such as the Rubbermaid Brilliance, is described as stain resistant, and glass such as the KOMUEE resists it best. Rinse promptly to reduce staining. Glass such as the KOMUEE and Vtopmart resists staining best, and the Rubbermaid Brilliance Tritan is described as stain resistant, so choose those if tomato sauce is a regular.
